sources.citation: Marlo, Michael R. 2013. Verb tone in Bantu languages: micro-typological patterns and research methods. Africana Linguistica 19: 137-234 (Persee pages 160-161, 181, 188 read online)
sources.note: Cites Fuliiru (Van Otterloo 2011) for reversive tone, OM tones, causative/passive tonal effects and reduplication tone domain; the only stress remark on those pages concerns Swahili, not Fuliiru.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Fuliiru only for /H/, /L/, /0/ verb-root contrast (Van Otterloo 2014:386); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Michaud, Alexis & Jacqueline Vaissiere. 2015. Tone and intonation: introductory notes and practical recommendations. KALIPHO 3 (halshs-01091477).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Kifuliiru (Van Otterloo 2011) only as an example of heavy morphological tone with straightforward phonetic implementation; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Van Otterloo, Roger. 2015. Fuliiru Narrative Discourse. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 32. Dallas: SIL International. 173 pp. (via Internet Archive copy of SIL PDF)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; 'prominence' used only in the discourse sense (emphatic prominence marker -ag); appendix on pauses, downdrift and sentence intonation.

sources.citation: Van Otterloo, Karen. 2014. Tonal melodies in the Kifuliiru verbal system. Africana Linguistica 20: 385-403. doi:10.3406/aflin.2014.1041 (Persee; PDF captcha-blocked, full text scraped page by page)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No statement on stress/accent. Says contour tones occur exclusively in the penult, every penult receives a second tone node before tone assignment (p.387); phrase-final H realized as short fall (L% boundary); long vowels shorten when followed by 3+ morae in the word. Tone (H/L/toneless roots, melodic TAM tones) only.

sources.note: Summarises ch. 2 (segmental phonology, syllable structure, cliticization) and ch. 3 (tone, final-syllable extratonality, mid tone); does not mention stress, accent or syllable prominence.

sources.note: Fuliiru cited for contrastive vowel length in any position (kuhaana 'give' vs kuhana 'punish'), vowel height, consonants; no stress statement for Fuliiru.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Fuliiru language' (current wikitext, based on Van Otterloo 2011a/b)
sources.note: Consonants, vowels (phonemic length), tone (H/L, mid = LH, falling = HL or utterance-final H); silent on stress.
